newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algerian president to keep same PM, says newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian president to keep same PM, says newspaper.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual is to keep his incumbent Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia in office to bolster government stability after last week's general election, a leading Algerian newspaper said on Monday.
The report coincided with a dispute among foreign observers over the fairness of the general election, the first after five years of violence, which brought opposition charges of vote rigging.
The Constitutional Council said on Monday it had endorsed the results announced last Friday, thus making them official.

These gave pro-government parties a majority in Algeria's first multi-party parliament. The council now has the task of deciding whether opposition parties' complaints were justified. It has nine days in which to make its decision.

A statement from some observers, published by local newspapers on Monday, said some had had problems moving freely while monitoring the poll, and there were questions over voting by security forces and at mobile polling stations.
But the head of the Indian observers' delegation, named only as Singh, denounced the statement as "not objective".
He told reporters in Algiers: "It is a report drawn up by four observers alone and does not represent the report of the United Nations mission."
In New York, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said the statement was not put out by the United Nations but an international group of election monitors not under U.N. control.

He said: "The U.N. has no role in assessing the validity of the elections. We have a small group of four people who were consultants. There was an international group of election monitors that was not under U.N. authority and it was those people who issued a communique today."

Most opposition parties said last Thursday's election was rife with irregularities. The ballot was dominated by the National Democratic Rally (RND) which took 155 seats in the 380-seat Assembly. Ouyahia and several ministers stood on the RND ticket.
El Khabar daily, quoting what it called informed sources, said Ouyahia would hand in his government's resignation to Zeroual on Monday.

Zeroual would then reinstal him as head of a new reshuffled government, the paper said, adding that Finance and Oil Ministers Abdelkrim Harchaoui and Ammar Makhloufi were likely to stay in their posts.
A senior official told Reuters Zeroual would name a prime minister in the "next hours". He said Zeroual was entitled by the constutition to name a head of government or keep the incumbent one.
The official results, now confirmed, gave the Islamist- oriented Movement for a Peaceful Society (MPS) 69 seats and its ally the Islamist Nahda Movement 34 seats.

The formerly ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) had 64 seats and the secularist Socialist Forces Front (FFS) and Rally for Culture and Democracy (RCD) 19 each. Independents and other small groups shared the remaining seats.

The observers' statement issued in Algiers said: "While observers were able to move without fear or threats, several had difficulties to carry out their work with all the independence and free movement necessary to assess objectively these elections."
It also said observers questioned what happened in the special voting bureaux where security forces cast their ballots early.
"The majority of observers who supervised them share the opinion that the process did not provide sufficient guarantees for neutrality and transparency," the statement said.
The Assembly will hold a maiden session on June 15 to elect the house speaker, party and official sources said.
Officials said the government would step up reforms, agreed upon with the International Monetary Fund, after the election, including a huge privatisation of state-owned enterprises.
